exercises.title: Skim the article (Ex. 13–14)
exercises.instruction: Read the introduction and the article quickly and answer the questions.

stimulus.text: A summer job will give you the chance to earn money and get some work experience, as well as learn new skills. Many teenagers think that it will be difficult to find a job because they don't have as much experience as an adult. However, that's not the case at all. Many employers like to give jobs to young people because they have lots of energy and enthusiasm. Before you apply for a job, make a list of the skills you have so you can write them on your application form. Not sure which job would be best for you? Here are some ideas to get you started.

exercises.title: Questions and answers with can (G&V Ex. 7–8)

items.prompt: A: ____ play sport?
B: Yes, ____ play basketball.
A: Not really, ____ play many sports, but I like watching them on TV.

exercises.title: Write an email applying for a summer job (Ex. 17, 20–21)
exercises.instruction: You have received an email about summer jobs. Write an email to Simon Stone (the summer jobs coordinator) to apply for ONE job in the article (sports coach, helping elderly people, fashion sales assistant, lifeguard, digital designer). In your email: (1) say which job you are interested in; (2) say what skills and abilities you have; (3) say which skill you couldn't do before but can do now. Write 60–80 words with a polite greeting and ending.

checklist: Nói rõ công việc muốn ứng tuyển
Nêu kỹ năng trước đây chưa có nhưng nay đã có (couldn't… but now I can…)
Mở đầu Dear Simon, kết thư lịch sự + tên
Không thêm thông tin ngoài đề
rubric.sampleAnswer:
Dear Simon,

I'm interested in the sports coach job at the summer camp.

I can play football and basketball well, and I'm good at teaching younger children because I often help my little cousins with their homework. I can also work long hours outside.

When I was younger, I couldn't talk to new people easily because I was very shy. Now I can make friends quickly, so I think I can work well in a team.

Best wishes,
Mai
commonErrors: Dùng could cho khả năng hiện tại
Quên ý 3 (kỹ năng trước chưa có)
Kể thêm thông tin không được yêu cầu

exercises.title: What is in Laura's email? (Ex. 18–19)
exercises.instruction: Read Laura's email (an application for a hotel receptionist job). Which features does it HAVE and which does it NOT have?

stimulus.text:
Dear Simon,

I'm interested in the hotel receptionist job. I think I have good skills to be a hotel receptionist. I could talk to new people easily and I could speak three languages – English, Spanish and Arabic. I can't work long hours but I want to learn this. I have a lot of experience. When I was younger, I worked in a restaurant.

Thanks,
Laura
stimulus.caption: Laura's email

categories.label: No – it does not have this

items.text: She says which job she is interested in.
She says what skills she has.
She says what skills she didn't have in the past but does now.
items.explanation: Laura viết "I can't work long hours but I want to learn this" — không phải kỹ năng quá khứ.

items.text: She uses a good structure – greeting to start the email and ends with her name.
She uses correct and appropriate grammar.
items.explanation: "I could talk… I could speak" phải là can (hiện tại).

items.text: She only talks about the information in the instructions.
items.explanation: Thêm chuyện làm nhà hàng — không được yêu cầu.

items.text: She uses the correct number of words.

exercises.title: Speaking: your skills and abilities (Ex. 9–11)
exercises.instruction: Answer each question in 20–30 seconds. Use can / can't / could / couldn't and add a reason and an example.

items.prompt: What are your best skills and abilities?
items.sampleAnswer: I think my best skill is remembering information. For example, I can learn twenty new English words in an evening and still remember them the next week. I'm also quite good at drawing, because I practise every weekend.
items.sampleNote: Kỹ năng + ví dụ cụ thể + lý do.

items.prompt: What skills do you want to learn?
items.sampleAnswer: I'd really like to learn how to cook, because at the moment I can only make instant noodles! My mum is a great cook, so I want to learn some traditional dishes from her, like spring rolls.
items.sampleNote: Mong muốn + lý do + ví dụ.

items.prompt: What skills and abilities did you have when you were younger?
items.sampleAnswer: When I was younger, I could swim really well – I was in the school swimming team. I could also play the piano a little, but I stopped when I started secondary school.

items.prompt: What skills did you NOT have when you were younger?
items.sampleAnswer: I couldn't talk to new people easily because I was very shy. For example, I never spoke in class. Now I can give presentations in front of my classmates, although I still feel a bit nervous.
items.sampleNote: couldn't → now I can: cho thấy sự tiến bộ.
